newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $68, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $68, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Friday were quiet, with light bids of $67.00 to $68.00 per cwt passed by owners asking $69.00 to $70.00, feedlot sources said.
Activity was expected to stay light going into the monthly USDA Cattle-On-Feed reports scheduled for release at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT Friday.
Most of this week's showlists were sold out at $69.00, up $2.00 from the bulk of last week's sales, although there were a few sales Thursday at $68.00 for lighter-weight cattle, some sources noted.

The pre-report average of analysts' estimates for USDA's report pegged the number of cattle on feed in the seven primary states on April 1 at 107.6 percent of a year ago, March placements at 103.3 percent of a year ago and March marketings at 100.6 percent.
Several feedlot sources said they expected placements to match or exceed the average estimate.

But cattle feeders were reluctant to project outlooks for next week's cattle prices until the report is released. Higher beef prices this week powered advances in fed cattle values, but ideas that prices were near a top may weaken values.
